correctness.rationale: Each minimal contract edge is itself a minimal obstruction span. Picking a pair that differs at its subfamily-private coordinate gives an identity minor on the chosen private coordinates, hence independent pair differences over F₂, in a difference space of dimension at most |C|−1. This proves the bound regardless of hypothesis count. The zero and edge-indicator contexts are distinct; exact guards ensure that each context has precisely the prescribed singleton explanation family, with no cross-context Horn-rule interference. All dependencies go from sources and hypotheses to terminal heads. Only zero-to-edge pairs are minimal obstructions and the antichain retains all their spans. Without any hypotheses, either no obstruction exists or a singleton obstruction forces the empty edge. In the globally private case, |C|=m+1 and the m independent pair differences exclude repeated pairs and cycles (differences telescope modulo two), giving a spanning tree. For disjoint labels on an arbitrary tree, XOR path assignments are distinct and an opposite-color pair has span the union of its path labels. Adjacent pairs realize every edge and all other opposite-color pairs give supersets; no converse for overlapping labels is asserted. RESULT.md proof steps 1–4 replay these arguments. I read VERIFICATION.md and checker.py without executing the latter. The checks enumerate small antichains, restricted two-choice tables and small labeled trees; the universal result comes from the proof, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a resource bound for realizing natural observation contracts, rather than another realizability proof. Private coordinates give a computable structural reason why adding more explanation atoms cannot reduce contexts below a threshold, with exact equality on a natural family and a tangible necessary witness tree. The optimal one-atom construction and disjoint-label tree family add explicit economical realizations. The result does not require the lower bound to be sharp on arbitrary overlapping contracts.
